text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Senior officials of ASEAN and the European Union working on positive aspects of their relations at meeting in Singapore despite sharp differences over human rights issues.
- Chinese New Year and Hari Raya Puasa take on special meaning when two sisters given away to different families when they were children are reunited after more than 50 years.
- Tamil Tiger guerillas raze police post in eastern Sri Lanka, killing 16 constables as tensions mount between minority Tamil and Muslim communites.
- Russia could use nuclear weapons first if under sufficient threat from a conventional army, senior security official says in newspaper interview.
- Property magnate Ng Teng Fong strengthening hold in prime residential area of Cairnhill.
- US economic expansion should continue into foreseeable future, says annual report on economy released by White House.
- Flush money market liquidity, thin trading conditions and ringgit's return to favour combine to drag down Singapore dollar against U.S. counterpart, foreign exchange dealers say.
- India may modify civil aviation policy to back foreign firms, step that will boost the chances of proposed Singapore $960 million Singapore Airlines-Tata joint venture.
- Asia will remain priority destination of investments by American manufacturers in next five years, recent survey says.
- Authorised motor traders ready to go head-to-head aganst parallel importers by entering parallel importing business themselves if their main agency lines cease to be viable.
- Retailers in U.S. get together to challenge Visa and MasterCard in anti-trust suit that potentially could cost the defendants billions of dollars.
- Electronics and plastics group Omni Industries expected to launch initial public offer of about 40 million to 50 million new shares on Singapore second board by month-end.
- Rafiq Jumabhoy's share option, entitling him to take over Jumabhoy family's 100 million Scotts Holdings shares, comes under attack from an expert witness.
- Malaysian groups target Australian companies to help further regional healthcare ambitions.
